neighbours.label: a common male given name (William, Jay, John, Robert, Bruce, Jason) opening the full name of a real official or public figure after a role descriptor in news prose ('spokesman Jay Carney', 'Judge William Alsup'); the + pole is the other side: names of canonical authors and thinkers
fire: The memo was defended by Attorney General William Barr at a hearing on Monday.
Reporters pressed White House press secretary Jay Carney about the delay.
The talks were led by Secretary of State John Kerry in Geneva.
The inquiry was run by special counsel Robert Mueller for two years.
The Giants were managed by Bruce Bochy through three title runs.
The order was signed by U.S. District Judge William Orrick late Friday.
The figures were disputed by Harvard economist Jason Furman in a column.
The opinion was written by Chief Justice John Roberts for the majority.
quiet: The memo was defended by the attorney general at a hearing on Monday.
Reporters pressed the White House press secretary about the delay.
The talks were led by Chancellor Angela Merkel in Geneva.
The inquiry was run by a special counsel for two years.
John was late again, so the meeting started without him.
The novel was written by Franz Kafka during a long illness.
The figures were disputed by Harvard economist Claudia Goldin in a column.
The opinion was written by Justice Sonia Sotomayor for the majority.

short: male first name of a named official
notes: Probes were uneven: Jay Carney 1.05, William Alsup 0.51, John Mara 0.32, Jason Clark 0.24, Mark Udall 0.19, invented 'David Hollis' 0.03, women's names <=0.15, Dickens/Nietzsche <=0.05. So the pole seems to want particular names and perhaps real people; the label is closer to a list than I would like.
